title: Building an Async Throne Room MMO with Replit— let’s see how it goes!
author: certaintyisuncertain
selftext:
I’m building an async space opera throne room MMO with Replit Agent and I want to see how far I can get.

Current workflow:

* Using Claude (app) to plan and scope instructions for Replit.
* Replit to build and host and deploy the code and environment.
* ChatGPT for image gen (although I think it is not great— so looking for alternatives here, eventually would love to work with a real artist for the character portraits.)

Recently I played through “Yes, Your Grace” and it was the first game I’ve actually finished in a long time. It inspired me to pick up this old idea that I got stuck on.

For some context on my experience: I’m not technical. I’ve been around dev work for most of my career but actually writing code is something I was never able to get the hang of. My background is web design, filmmaking, and marketing. I can write the absolute basic HTML/CSS (thanks MySpace) and hack things together with copy & pasted solutions from Stack Overflow (R.I.P.)

Last year though, for work, I spend 4 months in Replit on the side of the rest of my job and built a functioning email tool. A competitor to MailChimp/Constant Contact for our niche— it’s now being used to successfully send 10,000+ emails a month and approaching $2k/m in monthly recurring revenue.

So I’ve been very inspired by what Replit Agent can do. Sometimes very frustrated by its limitations lol, but most of those can be worked around.

So this is my plan: try my best over the next few months to build a working version 1 of this space opera Throne Room MMO… and see what happens.

I’ll share the progress (the good and bad) here. 

Happy to hear ideas on what would make a game like this exciting to you (if anything at all). In a few days I’ll share a post with more details about the gameplay and setting + more details on how I built what’s here so far.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Can you explain the concept a bit more? I'm not immediately sure what a throne room MMO looks like. The video is nice but doesnt make it clear how the MMO aspect works.

replies.author: certaintyisuncertain
replies.body:
Totally, the MMO aspect isn’t present yet— but that’s my goal. I have a lot of it mapped out, but won’t be building those aspects until I get single-player working and really fun.

I’m toying with the idea of it being a once per day game. Where you essentially take a turn every day. Then the server processes everyone’s turns and how the effect each other, and that influences what petitioners and events happen for you the next day.

Some version of that for sure, but still open to if that would be fun enough. For me, I think it would be great, especially if it works well or is primarily on mobile.

It already works that when you Charter a new House, you are generating a star system in the background that is populated uniquely (based on seeds and variation, not AI). It is next to an existing star system in the database, so you’re always next to another player, and over time it will expand outwards, meaning older players will be next to each other (ideally making it naturally harder) and new players will be generated on the outskirts of the map and be next to other relatively new players.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Thanks, so would players eventually be directly interacting with each other or just coexisting in the same world an influencing each other's playthroughs by altering the world?

replies.author: certaintyisuncertain
replies.body:
They will be able to directly interact with each other. That will be a major part of the gameplay is diplomacy with neighboring players. 

You can send letters and envoys to other players (not just your neighbors, it will just take a long time to get to other systems past there)— eventually will also be able to send military, spies, and traders as well.

comments.author: ZHName
comments.body:
I have a large suggestion. For more immersion, black background and white text. remove backgrounds on the characters and add a glow color behind each character to indicate status, condition, or whatever. This way focus is on imagination, and the beige color theme and simple fonts do not detract from the simple narrative driven game.

If possible, keep the menus out of the way so the choices of dialogue are seen on the same screen at once, without scrolling which breaks immersion and naturalness (this appears mobile oriented right?)

See if you can prototype a few different looks with my suggestion of a black bg and white text. Hide those menus or an expander button in the  bottom corner or top corner for additional things they dont need to see. Deepseek does good fast html mockups. 

The choices buttons should have a very nice tactile effect so that you really lean into some 'interaction' feeling whether that's tactile clickyness or gentle depression of the button so the user enjoys each interaction. 

This alone would elevate the game a little beyond a web pagey feel where its at right now.

replies.author: certaintyisuncertain
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback / ideas.

I have a couple of idea on how to make the design feel way cooler, but just wanted something that’s kind of in the right direction to start working through all the functionality first.

I’ll definitely take that feedback to mind when doing the next design pass. Good to know deepseek does good quick design mockups. I’ve found Claude does also, and I’m itching to try some other Claude skills to make them more varied.
